seo.title: Technical Consulting | Mohit Walia
seo.description: A practical read on architecture, stack, and the next build, written so a founder or a team can act on it.

hero.heading: Technical consulting before the expensive rewrite.
hero.subtitle: I review the product, the stack, and the plan, then leave you with a sequence you can build. Not a slide deck that avoids the hard part.

overview: Consulting is for a decision: what to build next, whether to rewrite, which stack to keep, or how to split a system that has tangled. The output is a written recommendation and a sequence.
problem: The team is busy shipping and the architecture questions keep getting postponed. A rewrite gets proposed because the current code feels uncomfortable, not because anyone mapped the cost.
solution: I read the code and the product, talk to the people who operate it, and write what to keep, what to change, and in what order. If a rebuild is the wrong spend, I will say that.

features.title: A written recommendation
features.detail: The decision, the reasons, and the risks in plain language.

features.title: A sequence
features.detail: What to do first so the team is not asked to boil the ocean.

features.title: Stack honesty
features.detail: Keep the tools that fit. Replace the ones that are costing you.

process.title: Discovery
process.detail: We pin down the outcome, the constraints, and what the first release has to do.

process.title: Planning
process.detail: I turn that into a scope, a sequence, and the technical approach.

process.title: Development
process.detail: I build in small slices you can review, on the stack this service uses.

process.title: Testing
process.detail: We check the flows that matter before anything is treated as finished.

process.title: Launch
process.detail: I ship it, watch the first days, and leave you with a clear way to change it.

benefits.title: The team can execute it
benefits.detail: The sequence is sized for the people you have.

benefits.title: Optional build help
benefits.detail: I can stay and implement the first slice, or stop at the writing.

deliverables: Risks and what you are choosing not to do
A call to walk through it

timeline.detail: Code, deploys, and a conversation with the people who feel the pain.
A call so the writing is not misread.

faqs.question: Is this an audit with a score?
faqs.answer: No. It is a recommendation tied to your product. I will not hand you a generic checklist with a grade.

faqs.question: Do you have to build it afterwards?
faqs.answer: No. The writing is useful on its own. Building the first slice is a separate agreement.
